checks.title: Problem-Solution Trace
checks.summary: Pitch claims '7,000+ transactions synthesized into coherent trading identity' implying deep synthesis/ML. Code is deterministic rule-based label-matching with 12 hardcoded if-then rules and lookup-table persona generation. The roast battle is pre-computed static content, not dynamic. The roast battle IS the demo hook, not the product — the product is shallow pattern classification dressed as theatrical identity revelation.
evidence: PRD.md:171 — 'Constraints: Rule-based (not ML), deterministic, runs in <2s for 7,000+ transactions' — explicitly admits no deep synthesis
src/lib/classifier.ts:3-14 — classifyPatterns() iterates 12 deterministic if-then rules (AMP-01 through GRD-06), each a simple threshold check on trade arrays
src/lib/persona.ts:2-7 — ARCHETYPES is a static lookup table mapping pattern IDs to hardcoded archetype strings. generatePersona() picks topAmp.id and does a dictionary lookup
src/lib/persona.ts:25-38 — generateCatchphrase() uses hardcoded if-else chains. Only 4 possible catchphrases exist
PRD.md Risk #5 — 'Pattern classifier produces LOW confidence on all tags' — mitigation: 'Insight comes from comparison, not algorithm depth' — self-admits the algorithm is shallow
PRD.md Risk #6 — 'Roast lines feel generic without live LLM generation' — mitigation: 'Pre-generate 2x needed lines' — roast content is static, not synthesized
src/data/cache/roast-lines.json — pre-computed static roast lines in cache
src/data/cache/roast-battle.json — pre-computed static battle data
DEMO-SCRIPT.md:15 — '[PRE-COMPUTED] Static roast lines in cache, not generated by LLM at runtime'
PRD.md:23 — '[PRE-COMPUTED] Pattern Data for Demo Wallets — AMPLIFY/GUARD tags pre-calculated, not from live OnchainOS queries'
checks.gap: The gap between '7,000+ transactions synthesized into coherent trading identity' and actual code: code maps each pattern ID to one of 6 archetype labels via a flat dictionary. No transaction-level reasoning, no cross-trade correlation, no behavioral synthesis. 'Coherent' identity = the single highest-confidence AMPLIFY tag determines archetype. This is label assignment, not synthesis.

checks.title: Architecture Diagram Honesty
checks.summary: ARCHITECTURE.md Section 1 System Diagram (lines 29-70) shows the full pipeline: Browser → Terminal Chat UI → Next.js API Routes → OnchainOS CLI Wrapper → Pattern Classifier → Persona Engine. It does NOT show the demo-mode short-circuit where OnchainOS is entirely bypassed and all data comes from pre-cached JSON files. The Data Flow section below the diagram (lines 168-180) does describe the cache path, but the visual diagram — the first thing a judge sees — is misleading.
evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:29-70 — System Diagram shows clean pipeline from Browser through OnchainOS CLI Wrapper to Pattern Classifier to Persona Engine. No demo-mode branch.
ARCHITECTURE.md:12-19 — Emergency Mode Notice table lists 3 mocked components (TEE, x402, Whale Monitoring) but does NOT list that the entire data pipeline is mocked/cached
ARCHITECTURE.md:168-180 — Data Flow section shows 'RUNTIME (demo): page.tsx → WalletInput → POST /api/analyze → cache.ts (loads pre-cached data)' — this is below the fold, after the diagram
src/app/api/analyze/route.ts:10-13 — 'if (process.env.DEMO_MODE === "true" || cacheExists()) { const cached = await loadAllDemoData(); ... }' — entire OnchainOS path is dead code when cache exists
src/lib/cache.ts:69-81 — loadAllDemoData() loads 7 pre-cached JSON files, bypassing classifier.ts and persona.ts entirely (patterns.json and personas.json are pre-computed)
src/app/page.tsx:15 — launchDemo uses hardcoded strings '0xDemo...' and 'SolDemo...' — no wallet lookup ever happens
src/app/api/roast/route.ts:6-7 — roast endpoint uses loadRoastBattle() which reads static JSON from cache
src/app/api/compare/route.ts:6-7 — compare endpoint uses loadComparison() which reads static JSON from cache
checks.gap: The System Diagram implies OnchainOS is always the data source. In reality, every API endpoint in demo mode reads from src/data/cache/*.json files. The diagram should show a 'Demo Mode' branch pointing to Cache Layer → direct response, sidestepping the entire pipeline.

checks.title: Value-Prop Chain Integrity
checks.finding: FALSE CLAIM DETECTED + MOCKED VALUE PROPS
checks.summary: The task asks about 'Depositors earn passive yield' — this claim does NOT exist anywhere in Alter Ego's docs or code. It is a phantom value prop not made by the project. The ACTUAL value props ('Know thyself', '$0.99 snapshot', 'TEE-sealed') all trace to code but every single one is mocked or shallow. The self-knowledge engine is deterministic label matching, the $0.99 payment is simulated, and the TEE attestation is a static badge.
evidence: DEPOSITORS/PASSIVE YIELD: grep across entire project (excl. node_modules/.next) for 'depositor|passive.*yield|earn.*yield|deposits' → ZERO matches in docs/source. This is not a value prop Alter Ego claims.

'Know thyself': README.md:3 'Self-knowledge is the product.' — src/app/page.tsx:48-50 — hero text includes 'Self-knowledge is the product.' — src/app/page.tsx:181 — CTA text: 'Alter Ego. Know thyself. Then know everyone else.' — BUT the persona engine (src/lib/persona.ts:2-7) is a static lookup table mapping pattern IDs to 6 hardcoded archetypes. No psychological modeling, no behavioral insight generation.

'$0.99 snapshot': README.md:59 '$0.99 per snapshot.' — src/app/page.tsx:181 '<PaymentButton tier="Snapshot" price="$0.99" />' — src/components/PaymentButton.tsx:4 — onClick sets state to 'simulating' for 1.5s then 'done' with text '✓ Payment Simulated'. No real payment. PRD.md:20 '[MOCK] Demo bypass + "Simulate Payment" button'

'TEE-sealed': README.md:22 'runs inside a TEE (Trusted Execution Environment).' — src/app/page.tsx:113-115 — static badge '🔒 ATTESTATION: 0x7f3a...b91e' hardcoded in JSX. PRD.md:19 '[MOCK] Pre-computed badge, no live attestation.' — public/tee-badge.svg is a static SVG.
'Coaching subscription $4.99/mo': README.md:59 — mentioned in text. No code evidence whatsoever — no PaymentButton for coaching tier, no subscription logic, no route handler.
'Battle $1.99': PRD.md:46 — mentioned in pricing table. No code evidence for battle payment tier.
checks.gap: Value-prop chain integrity is broken at every link: the 'self-knowledge' comes from a dictionary lookup, the $0.99 payment is simulated, the TEE seal is a static SVG, and two of four pricing tiers ($4.99/mo coaching, $1.99 battle) have zero code implementation.

checks.title: Target-Audience Coherence
checks.summary: Stated audience is crypto traders with multiple wallets across multiple chains. Code is a single-user demo with hardcoded addresses, no authentication, no session management, and shared global cache state. Cannot serve multiple simultaneous users.
evidence: src/app/page.tsx:15 — launchDemo passes hardcoded strings: '{ address: "0xDemo...", chains: ["ethereum"] }, { address: "SolDemo...", chains: ["solana"] }' — not real addresses, not configurable
grep across src/ for 'multi.?user|simultaneous|concurrent|session' → ZERO matches in 29 files

src/app/api/analyze/route.ts:10-21 — demo mode always returns the same cached data regardless of input addresses: 'const cached = await loadAllDemoData(); return NextResponse.json({ ... cached data ... })'
src/lib/cache.ts:9-10 — cache loads from global filesystem path 'src/data/cache/' — shared global state, no user isolation
No authentication middleware, no login page, no session tokens, no per-user database, no user context anywhere in the codebase
PRD.md:311 — demo wallets are 'TBD — select public leaderboard wallet' — confirms addresses are chosen once and baked in
README.md:42 — mentions 'Users paste any EVM or Solana address' — but the demo mode ignores whatever users paste and returns pre-cached data for the 3 hardcoded wallets
checks.gap: The code is structurally single-tenant. Multi-user would require: authentication layer, per-user session isolation, per-user cache/database, and removal of hardcoded demo addresses. None of this scaffolding exists. The demo can only ever show one story for one 'user' (the 3 pre-seeded wallets).

checks.title: Differentiator Authenticity
checks.summary: Claim 'Nobody is building a trading IDENTITY agent' is a hackathon-scope claim (comparing to other OKX.AI Genesis projects: Eat This?, WorldCupCaller, CertiK). The differentiation from market portfolio trackers (Zerion, Zapper, Nansen, Dune) is conceptual — 'they show balances, we show identity' — but the 'identity agent' is deterministic rule-based classification, not agentic or AI-driven. The persona+roast-battle concept IS unique as a hackathon demo format, but the claim 'trading IDENTITY agent' inflates a label-matching system into an 'agent.'
evidence: PRD.md:45 — 'Nobody is building a trading IDENTITY agent. Eat This? does food. WorldCupCaller does predictions. CertiK does security.' — competitors cited are all hackathon peers, not market incumbents

submission/DETAILS-BODY.html:34 — 'Existing portfolio trackers show balances. They do not tell you why you trade the way you do, or what it costs you.' — differentiation claim is conceptual, not verifiable from code
src/lib/persona.ts:2-7 — ARCHETYPES: 6 possible archetypes mapped from 6 AMPLIFY pattern IDs. The 'identity agent' is a flat dictionary lookup
src/lib/classifier.ts — 12 deterministic rules (6 AMPLIFY + 6 GUARD). No learning, no adaptation, no agentic behavior — purely static classification
No LLM integration, no ML model, no adaptive behavior, no stateful agent loop — grep for 'agent|llm|model|openai|anthropic' in src/ → ZERO relevant matches
Portfolio trackers (Zerion/Zapper): show balances + transaction history — Alter Ego adds pattern tags on top, which IS a differentiation, but the depth is shallow
Nansen/Dune: provide analytics dashboards with smart money labeling — Alter Ego's 'identity' concept is personified labels, not quantitative analytics depth
checks.gap: The persona+roast-battle format IS genuinely novel as a demo concept and the hackathon comparison may be accurate within scope. But calling it a 'trading IDENTITY agent' is misleading — it's a deterministic classifier with theatrical UI. The gap is between 'agent' (implies autonomous, learning, adaptive behavior) and 'static rule engine with pre-computed output.' For the hackathon, this is likely acceptable; for a production claim, it would not hold.

cross_cutting_themes: THE DEMO IS THE PRODUCT: Everything — persona generation, roast lines, pattern data, TEE attestation, payments — is pre-computed/mocked. The code serves a static 90-second theatrical experience, not a functioning product. The narrative is coherent AS A DEMO but would collapse under any live usage.

DEPTH vs THEATER DISCONNECT: The pitch narrative promises deep synthesis and agentic identity revelation. The code delivers deterministic label matching with pre-written output. The gap is consistently filled by the theatrical demo script and visual design, not by technical capability.

DOCUMENTATION DRIFT: README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, PRD.md, and DEMO-SCRIPT.md disagree on transaction counts (4,463 in DEMO-SCRIPT, 7,290 in PRD, 6,134 in page.tsx stats bar, '7,000+' in problem statement). The codebase has hardcoded values that vary across files.
sources_audited: src/data/cache/ — directory listing (9 JSON files present)
verdict: NARRATIVE INFLATION — The pitch, docs, and demo narrate a story of deep AI-driven identity synthesis. The code delivers a deterministic 12-rule classifier with lookup-table persona assignment, serving entirely pre-computed static data. The demo is a well-crafted theatrical experience but the technical claims ('7,000+ transactions synthesized into coherent trading identity', 'TEE-bound agent', 'trading IDENTITY agent') significantly overstate the actual implementation.
